# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

```text
# Poodle — Video Agent for Incident & Insurance Claims

> Real-Time Video Agents Hack · VAST London · 17 Oct 2026
> Theme fit: an agent that **searches footage, answers questions, spots events, and takes action**.
> Judging criteria (VAST blog): **creativity, technical implementation, real-world impact**.

Poodle is the name of this idea. The claims desk is [`poodle/index.html`](../poodle/index.html). A small apricot poodle sits on top of that desk and moves with the open claim: steady while you read, brighter when a decision is ready for a person to confirm. The desk writes that same mood in words, so the motion is not the only signal.

## One-liner

When a road incident happens, Poodle takes every piece of footage (dashcam, CCTV, phone clips), the GPS track, the location context and the claimant's insurance policy. It reconstructs what happened on one synced timeline, answers an adjuster's questions with timestamped clip proof, checks the events against the road rules, flags contradictions and fraud signals, **decides whether the claim is covered and which benefits apply** (accept, partial, reject or refer to a human), and exports a tamper-evident evidence pack fit to share with lawyers or a court.

## Problem

- Motor claims depend on "he said / she said". Video exists more often than ever (dashcams, doorbells, shop CCTV, phones), but adjusters still scrub through it by hand.
- Clips arrive from different devices, with different clocks, angles and quality. Nobody lines them up.
- Liability depends on context the video alone doesn't show: junction layout, signal phases, speed limits, give-way lines, the Highway Code.
- Even once fault is clear, the adjuster still has to read the policy: is this peril covered under the customer's cover level, does an exclusion apply, which benefits (courtesy car, windscreen, legal expenses, personal injury) kick in, what is the excess. This is slow, inconsistent between handlers, and hard to explain to the customer.
```

```text
# Hack plan: VAST Builders Challenge London, 17 October 2026

Written at 12:00 BST. Build ends at 16:30 BST. Demos start at 16:30. Awards at 18:30.
Status: the research is complete. The idea panel and the adversarial novelty check are still running. This file will be updated when they report.

## 1. Decision now

Build **RackWitness**: a camera agent that watches a technician install a GPU or storage node against the vendor runbook, flags a wrong cable or a skipped step within seconds, and writes a timestamped commissioning record with evidence clips into VastDB.

Why this one:

- The sponsors in the room are the customers. CoreWeave racks tens of thousands of GPU nodes and runs VAST AI OS. VAST ships CNode and DNode hardware. NVIDIA deploys DGX SuperPODs.
- It reuses the PC-build demo from your second inspiration. A PC case on the bench plays a 1U node.
- It hits all four judges: temporal step tracking (NVIDIA), one data platform for clips, events and search (VAST x2), a Weave eval with numbers (W&B).
- No team in San Francisco or New York built it.

Runner-up: **ClearTray**, a security-lane divest coach. It keeps the airport spirit of your first inspiration. See section 5.

## 2. How the room scores

The only published criteria are **creativity, technical implementation and real-world impact** (Ram Bansal, VAST blog, 18 Aug 2026). The first round is a table walkthrough with each team. The 3-minute demo and the recorded video are the product.

| Judge | What they ship or study | Show them | Do not show them |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Abubakr Karali, NVIDIA Senior Solutions Architect | Computer-vision researcher: action recognition, tracking, multi-camera. Ex Metropolis EMEA and Smart Spaces. Reshared VSS 3 "agentic search for actions and temporal events". | State tracked across frames, YOLO track IDs that gate the VLM, Cosmos 2D points on the frame, honest precision and latency. | Per-frame captions sold as "video understanding", one cherry-picked clip, no false-positive handling. |
| Ram Bansal, VAST Sr Developer Advocate | Wrote the reference pipeline the lab runs. Ships open-source repos and MCP servers. | A clean repo that reproduces the demo, the agent exposed as an MCP tool, own rows in VastDB. | A search box. He has seen it at two cities. |
| Brian Verkley, VAST Director AI Data Platform (keynote) | AgentEngine author. Thesis: keep all data in one place, let agents observe, reason, act, evaluate. | Clips, detections, verdicts and search in one platform. An action with a cost or safety value. "In production this is a DataEngine trigger." | A laptop frontend that calls one API with no data layer. Sponsor tools bolted on. |
| Junaid Butt, W&B AI Solutions Engineer | Evals person. Judged the Mistral London hack for W&B. Promotes AI-evals courses. | Weave traces with the frame attached, a 20-item labelled eval, a leaderboard, before-and-after numbers. | "It works" with no numbers. W&B used only as a token endpoint. |

Winning mechanics at sibling video hacks (Neo4j and TwelveLabs hack, July 2026; NVIDIA Cosmos Cookoff): finished live demo, answers linked to timestamps and clips, deterministic verification around the VLM, typed outputs, a reframed domain.

## 3. Stack facts you need today

- Lab pipeline: S3 chunks -> Segmenter (5 s) -> YOLO11s detector -> Cosmos3-Reason reasoner -> Cosmos Embed1 (256-dim) -> VastDB. Only Detector -> Reasoner -> Embedder re-runs during the day. Do not redeploy the DataEngine graph.
- Direct model calls from the team VM: Cosmos3-Reason at `$COSMOS3_REASON_URL/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI format, clip as `data:video/mp4;base64`, 4 fps default, ask for `<think>` and `<answer>` JSON, `max_tokens` small). YOLO at `$YOLO_URL/v1/infer` with `video_base64`. Cosmos Embed1 at `$COSMOS_EMBED1_URL/v1/embeddings`. Canary-1B ASR at `$CANARY_1B_URL/v1/audio/transcriptions`. Check `/config/<team>.config` for a bearer token. The docs disagree on auth.
- VSS API (JWT from `/api/v1/auth/login`): `POST /api/v1/search` (hybrid, `metadata_filters`, `time_filter`), `POST /api/v1/agent/ask`, `POST /api/v1/videos/upload` (own `.mp4` or `.webm`, `scenario`, `custom_prompt` <= 800 chars), `POST /api/v1/dashboard/reingest`, `POST /api/v1/videos/synthesize`.
- VastDB: `vastdb` Python SDK with PyArrow. Make your own schema and table, for example `commissioning.events`. Never drop `vss-collection`.
- W&B serverless inference: `https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1`, OpenAI client with `project=`. Text models: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B`, `meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct`. Vision models exist too (Gemma 4, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL). Weave: `weave.init`, `@weave.op`, `weave.Evaluation`, leaderboards.
- Corpus: highway I-24, Toronto dashcam, neighborhood cam, SF streets, warehouse (~178 clips), indoor smart space (~102 clips). Internet video is banned. Own local recordings are allowed by the upload skill. Confirm with Ram before you rely on it.
- Deploy: Python or Node app under 1 MiB of code, port 8080, team namespace, open from the App button. A laptop-only app does not count.
- Known risks from NYC and SF: re-ingest stalls for 40 minutes or more, pods restart, the shared GPU adds seconds. Keep local copies of every clip. Build a replay mode.
- Cosmos Reason2-8B accepts about 42 percent of non-events (PERJURY team benchmark). Put a deterministic check around every VLM verdict.

## 4. The two inspirations

### Airport X-ray or lidar detection

Verdict: **crowded and no data**. SeeTrue holds ECAC certification since January 2026. Smiths iCMORE, Rapiscan and Leidos ship the same product. STING-BEE (CVPR 2025) already does VLM reasoning on X-ray images. The lab corpus has no X-ray or lidar footage. Cosmos was not trained on X-ray. Do not build this.

Keep the spirit: point the agent at the security lane, not the scanner. That is ClearTray in section 5.

### Smart-glasses "expert eyes"

Verdict: **partially taken**. Meta Live AI, Gemini Live and ChatGPT voice-and-video answer questions about what the camera sees. Factory systems (Retrocausal, PTC Step Check, iFactory) verify steps from fixed station cameras. Understudy (SF team 39) coached a person live from expert clips on this exact stack.

Open ground: proactive interruption only on a mistake, grounding in a written runbook with no expert video, retrofit onto wearable or archived footage, and a searchable evidence record. RackWitness takes that ground for the buyer with the most money in the room.

## 5. Candidate ideas

| Idea | Source | Buyer tomorrow | Demo moment | Real problem | Sellable | Novel | Sponsor pain | Score |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RackWitness | Claude panel | Vendor professional services, neocloud build teams, install contractors | Orange cable goes into FABRIC-1 instead of MGMT. Flag within 5 s with the port circled. Search all install footage for the same error. | yes | yes | likely, check pending | yes, CoreWeave and VAST | 8.5 |
| ClearTray | Claude panel | Airport screening operators, lane vendors | Judge drops a bag with the laptop inside. "Please take your laptop out of the bag." Then: every tray this morning that failed divest. | yes | yes, slow procurement | likely, check pending | NVIDIA Smart Spaces | 8 |
| Lone Job | Cursor | Facilities operations director | Tool left on the frame before the panel closes. One sentence. The old job video plays at the same second. | yes | yes | partial | VAST archive thesis | 7.5 |
| Return Stop | Cursor | Head of returns at a hardware company | 16 of 20 return videos show open memory clips. Live build stops before power-on. | yes | yes | partial | VAST archive thesis | 7 |
| QuietHands | Claude panel | No clear buyer | Grandmother builds a PC. The coach speaks only on a mistake. | yes | no | partial | NVIDIA, W&B | 6.5 |

The Cursor ideas are in `docs/cursor-hack-ideas.md`. Lone Job and RackWitness share the same loop. RackWitness has the richer buyer and the judges' own employers as customers.

## 6. Build plan for RackWitness (4.5 hours)

Team: two people. Web demo only. No accounts, no mobile app, no second agent.

### Props

- One PC case or motherboard on the bench. Print large port labels: MGMT, FABRIC-1, PSU-A, PSU-B.
- Three cable colours. One ESD strap. One RAM stick or drive.
- An 8-step runbook as text. Example: strap on, rails, drives in order, PSU-A, PSU-B, orange cable to MGMT, blue cable to FABRIC-1, scan label.

### Schedule

| Time | Who | Do this |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12:00-12:30 | Both | Set up props. Write the runbook. Send it to W&B inference to get a JSON step graph: step id, expected visible evidence, cable colour to port map, known mistakes. Confirm own-footage upload with Ram. |
| 12:30-13:15 | A | Record 8 takes on a phone from above: 4 correct, 4 with one planted error. Keep local copies. Upload them with `scenario: egocentric`, `camera_id: headcam_tech1` and a custom prompt that names the labels, cable colours and parts. |
| 12:30-14:00 | B | Backend (FastAPI, port 8080). Browser posts 4-second webm clips. YOLO gates on person or hands present. Cosmos3-Reason gets the clip, the current step, the next step and the cable map. It returns JSON: step id, status (done, not done, deviation), evidence timestamp, 2D point, explanation. Advance the state only when two consecutive windows agree. Write each event to `commissioning.events` in VastDB. |
| 14:00-15:00 | A | UI: live camera with the circled point, runbook checklist, commissioning record, "sign-off and punch list" button (W&B LLM), search panel on `POST /api/v1/search` with `metadata_filters {camera_id: headcam_tech1}`. |
| 14:00-15:00 | B | Weave: `@weave.op` on YOLO, Cosmos and LLM calls with the frame attached. Label 20 windows. Run `weave.Evaluation` with gate on and off. Publish a leaderboard. |
| 15:00-15:45 | Both | Deploy with `/deploy-app-no-registry`. Record the 3-minute video with replay mode. Write the README with the architecture and the five sponsor tools. |
| 15:45-16:15 | Both | Rehearse the pitch twice out loud. Fix one thing only. |
| 16:15-16:30 | A | Submit: repo, video link, description, tools, names, emails. |

### Cuts

- No voice input unless everything else works by 15:00. Canary ASR is a stretch.
- No Cosmos critic second pass unless the deviation flag misfires in tests.
- No consumer framing. Say "grandmother" only as a one-line origin story.

### Fallbacks

- If upload or re-ingest stalls: compute Cosmos Embed1 vectors yourself and run kNN over `commissioning.events` in Python.
- If the GPU is slow: shorter clips, `max_tokens` 256, a visible "verifying step 6" state, replay mode.
- If Cosmos cannot tell the ports apart: make the rule "orange cable goes to the port with the big MGMT label". Use large labels and a static camera.

## 7. Where Jev fits (stretch, not required)

Jev is TypeSafe's typed decision model (see the `jev-decisions` skill). It is not a sponsor tool. Use it only if a key is available, and only in these spots:

- Verifier vote: send the frame still and the Cosmos explanation. Ask one Noul: "Does the frame show the orange cable in the MGMT port?" Combine it with the YOLO gate and the two-window rule into a quorum. This counters the Cosmos yes-bias at about 100 ms.
- Action gate: one Choice, allow / deny / escalate, before the agent writes a red flag or a sign-off.
- Box: locate "the orange cable end" when Cosmos returns no point.

Script: `.agents/skills/jev-decisions/scripts/jev_video_triage.py`. No TypeSafe or OpenRouter key is in the environment yet.

## 8. Pitch (3 minutes)

1. Problem (30 s): "Every GPU node goes in by hand. One swapped port costs hours at bring-up. The head-cam footage exists and nobody watches it." Name CoreWeave and VAST field services as the people who have this problem.
2. Live moment (90 s): the judge plugs the orange cable into the wrong port. The flag appears with the port circled. The judge fixes it. The record shows "corrected 00:58".
3. The archive (30 s): search "cable inserted into wrong port" across the day's takes. Show the Weave leaderboard: precision with and without the gate.
4. Why now and ask (30 s): "Same loop, swap the webcam for the tech's head-cam, same runbook format. It runs on a DGX Spark on the build cart." Ask for a pilot on one build cart.

Map each beat to a criterion out loud: creativity (a witness, not a search box), technical implementation (gate, verify, two-window rule, VastDB, Weave), real-world impact (rework hours and outages).

## 9. Sanity checks

1. Who pays tomorrow: vendor professional-services arms and neocloud build teams.
2. Sellable Monday: yes, as per-node commissioning records on one build cart.
3. Exact match exists: no. Two web searches at 12:05 ("AI camera verifies data center technician rack installation cabling steps runbook commissioning record video" and "wearable camera vision language model step verification technician procedure deviation alert product") found no product. Closest: ACSETRA validates commissioning photos and tags, not video or steps (https://acsetra.com/solutions/ai-data-center-commissioning). Factory systems are fixed-station. The adversarial check in the workflow is still pending.
4. Whose pain: CoreWeave (W&B's parent), VAST, NVIDIA.
5. 30-second moment: the wrong port flagged and circled.
6. Cut if 2 hours are lost: voice, critic pass, leaderboard. Keep gate, verdict, record, search.
7. Headline: "A witness for every node you rack."
8. The winner in the room probably builds another warehouse or traffic agent. This is more defensible.
9. Picked to win, not to build.

# Two ideas for the VAST Builders Challenge London

Date: 17 October 2026. Build window ends at 16:30.
This file is independent of Claude's hack plan.

## How the room will score

The project must use at least 3 sponsor tools and must play in a 3-minute demo.
Use a web page. Do not build a phone app.

Brian Verkley, Director, AI Data Platform at VAST Data, writes that the agent and the data must share one platform. A demo that reasons on one clip, with no stored video, misses his test.
Source: https://www.vastdata.com/blog/the-camp-stack-a-new-developer-stack-for-ai

Abubakr Karali, Senior Solutions Architect at NVIDIA, works on action recognition and video language models. He has already seen city cameras, smart spaces, and warehouse video.
Source: https://info.nvidia.com/vlm-webinar.html

Ram Bansal, Developer Advocate at VAST Data, has already published video search: ingest, summarize, embed, and search.
Source: https://www.vastdata.com/blog/unlock-video-intelligence-build-real-time-video-search-and-ai-summary

Junaid Butt, AI Solutions Engineer at Weights & Biases, says the value sits in the chain around the model. Show that chain.
Source: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/junaid-butt-23a18314a_a-bit-late-but-two-weekends-ago-i-had-the-activity-7436754736994959360-7C4t

NVIDIA Cosmos Reason can judge space, time, and the next physical step.
Source: https://docs.nvidia.com/cosmos/latest/reason2/index.html

NVIDIA already ships a warehouse safety agent that writes incident reports. Do not copy it.
Source: https://docs.nvidia.com/vss/latest/warehouse-docs/agents.html

## Idea 1 — Lone Job

### Use-case

A facilities firm maintains the air-conditioning plant on office roofs. One engineer does the night visit. He is alone in the plant room.

Last month, an engineer closed a metal access panel with a screwdriver still on the frame. The fan struck the tool. The motor failed. The firm has that night's body-camera video in storage. Nobody watched the video until the motor invoice arrived.

Tonight, a second engineer does the same job. He wears a camera. For the demo, the camera is the laptop webcam, and a cardboard box is the panel.

He changes the filter. The web page stays blank. He sets the screwdriver on the frame and reaches for the panel screws. The page then shows one sentence: "Stop. The tool is still on the frame." Beside the sentence, the old video plays at the second where the first engineer lifts the screwdriver out and then closes the panel.

He picks up the screwdriver. He closes the panel. The page goes blank again.

The operations director pays for this. One missed tool can cost a motor, a return visit, and an injury report. The director already pays for a lone-worker alarm. That alarm only sends help after the engineer presses a button. This agent watches the job.

### The buyer

The buyer is the operations director at a facilities or maintenance firm. The firm already pays for lone-worker alarms. Those alarms do not look at the job. A bad close-up becomes a return visit, an injury, or a claim.

This work helps lone workers. There are more than 1 million lone workers worldwide. The employer can buy a pilot on one contract.

### The 30-second moment

The page is quiet. The webcam shows a small panel, played by a box and a tool. The engineer leaves the tool inside and moves to close the lid. The agent says: "Stop. The tool is still inside." The page shows an old frame from a stored job, where the tool came out before the lid closed.

The silence is the product. The agent speaks once.

### Why the archive matters

The agent has no written procedure. The standard is the last good job in storage. VAST search finds that moment. Cosmos Reason judges the live step and the risk. YOLO tracks the hand, the tool, and the lid. A Weights & Biases model writes the one sentence. The trace on the page shows the chain: search, judgment, sentence.

### What already exists

CareAR, Augmentir, and skillia sell step guidance and skill scores from a planned lesson.
Sources: https://carear.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/SB-CareAR-Instruct-Digital-ENUS.pdf
https://www.augmentir.ai/product/augie-generative-ai-suite
https://skillia.ai/physical-work-skill-verification

ReSOP sells on-site answers from an approved procedure.
Source: https://www.resop.io/

Lone Job uses a different standard. The standard is old job video that nobody indexed. The page has no chat and no checklist.

### Build this

1. Film 4 short clips on a phone. Three clips show a correct close. One clip shows a tool left inside.
2. Put the clips in the video store and index them.
3. Build one web page: live view, one sentence, one old frame, one trace.
4. On the live view, Cosmos checks the lid and the tool. Search returns the correct old frame.
5. Show a Weights & Biases trace for the decision.
6. Record a 3-minute backup before 16:00.

### Leave this out

Do not build glasses, accounts, a mobile app, or a second agent. Do not show a search box.

## Idea 2 — Return Stop

### Use-case

A small PC company sells a desktop kit. Customers build it at home. In one week, 20 customers return the PC and say that it is dead. The warehouse tests the 20 PCs. Sixteen of them work when a technician pushes the memory card down until the two side clips click shut. Four PCs have a real board fault.

Each customer sent a short video with the return. The videos sit in a folder. The support team does not have time to watch them.

On Monday, the head of returns opens one web page. She does not type a question. The page says: "16 of 20 return videos show the same fault. The memory clips are open. 4 videos show a different fault." She can play the second where the clips are still up.

A new customer then starts a build on camera. For the demo, this customer is at the table, and the camera is the laptop webcam. She pushes the memory card in, but the side clips stay up. She moves her hand to the power button. The page says: "Stop. Close the memory clips before you switch the power on." It plays the old return video at the second where the clips click shut.

She closes the clips. She switches the power on. The PC starts. The company keeps the PC and the shipping cost.

The head of returns pays for this. She pays because 16 good PCs came back as dead.

### The buyer

The buyer is the head of returns at a hardware or appliance company. A no-fault return costs the product and the shipping. The company can buy a pilot on one product line.

### The 30-second moment

Five stored return videos sit on the page. Four show the same fault: the memory clips are open. The fifth shows a different fault. The agent names the repeated fault first. Then the webcam is the customer. Her hand moves to the power button. The agent says: "Stop. Seat the memory. The clips are open." It plays the matching second from an old return.

The grandmother story is the demo. The returns lead is the buyer.

### Why the archive matters

A guide would need an author. This agent has no guide. Cosmos Reason sees the open clips and the hand on the switch. VAST search finds the same state in stored returns. YOLO tracks the hand and the part. A Weights & Biases model writes the stop sentence. A small score on the page shows 4 of 5 test clips judged correctly.

### What already exists

Jiminy, Orus, and Blitzz guide one live support call.
Sources: https://usejiminy.com/
https://orusai.lovable.app/
```

```text
# Poodle — Video Agent for Incident & Insurance Claims

> Real-Time Video Agents Hack · VAST London · 17 Oct 2026
> Theme fit: an agent that **searches footage, answers questions, spots events, and takes action**.
> Judging criteria (VAST blog): **creativity, technical implementation, real-world impact**.

Poodle is the name of this idea. The claims desk is [`poodle/index.html`](../poodle/index.html). A small apricot poodle sits on top of that desk and moves with the open claim: steady while you read, brighter when a decision is ready for a person to confirm. The desk writes that same mood in words, so the motion is not the only signal.

## One-liner

When a road incident happens, Poodle takes every piece of footage (dashcam, CCTV, phone clips), the GPS track, the location context and the claimant's insurance policy. It reconstructs what happened on one synced timeline, answers an adjuster's questions with timestamped clip proof, checks the events against the road rules, flags contradictions and fraud signals, **decides whether the claim is covered and which benefits apply** (accept, partial, reject or refer to a human), and exports a tamper-evident evidence pack fit to share with lawyers or a court.

## Problem

- Motor claims depend on "he said / she said". Video exists more often than ever (dashcams, doorbells, shop CCTV, phones), but adjusters still scrub through it by hand.
- Clips arrive from different devices, with different clocks, angles and quality. Nobody lines them up.
- Liability depends on context the video alone doesn't show: junction layout, signal phases, speed limits, give-way lines, the Highway Code.
- Even once fault is clear, the adjuster still has to read the policy: is this peril covered under the customer's cover level, does an exclusion apply, which benefits (courtesy car, windscreen, legal expenses, personal injury) kick in, what is the excess. This is slow, inconsistent between handlers, and hard to explain to the customer.
...
```

```text
=====SERVICES=====
"""Sponsor-stack adapters. Each switches on from env vars; without them Poodle runs
in replay mode and reports that in /api/health.

Unverified against the event stack (no credentials on the build laptop): the YOLO,
Cosmos, W&B Inference, Jev and VastDB request shapes follow docs/hack-plan.md and the
jev-decisions skill. Check them on the team VM before the demo.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EVENTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "events.jsonl"


def load_dotenv(path: Path) -> None:
    """Read KEY=VALUE lines into the environment. Variables already set win, blank values are skipped."""
    if not path.exists():
        return
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
        key = key.removeprefix("export ").strip()
        value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
        if key and value and key not in os.environ:
            os.environ[key] = value


load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")


def env(name: str) -> str | None:
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    return value.strip() if value and value.strip() else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- detector

_local_model = None


def _local_yolo_available() -> bool:
    try:
        import ultralytics  # noqa: F401
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False


LOCAL_YOLO = _local_yolo_available()


def _local_detect(image: bytes) -> list[dict]:
    global _local_model
    import io

    from PIL import Image
    from ultralytics import YOLO

    if _local_model is None:
        _local_model = YOLO(env("POODLE_YOLO_WEIGHTS") or "yolo11s.pt")
    img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(image)).convert("RGB")
    w, h = img.size
    pred = _local_model.predict(img, conf=0.25, verbose=False)[0]
    out = []
    for box, cls, conf in zip(pred.boxes.xyxy.tolist(), pred.boxes.cls.tolist(), pred.boxes.conf.tolist()):
        x1, y1, x2, y2 = box
        out.append({"label": pred.names[int(cls)], "conf": round(float(conf), 3),
                    "box": [round(x1 / w, 4), round(y1 / h, 4), round((x2 - x1) / w, 4), round((y2 - y1) / h, 4)]})
    return out


async def detect(client: httpx.AsyncClient, image: bytes) -> dict:
    started = time.perf_counter()
    url = env("YOLO_URL")
    if url:
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {env('YOLO_TOKEN')}"} if env("YOLO_TOKEN") else {}
        r = await client.post(f"{url.rstrip('/')}/v1/infer", headers=headers, timeout=20,
                              json={"image_base64": base64.b64encode(image).decode()})
        r.raise_for_status()
        body = r.json()
        dets = body.get("detections") or body.get("predictions") or []
        return {"source": "YOLO (event stack)", "ms": round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000), "detections": dets}
    if LOCAL_YOLO:
        dets = await asyncio.to_thread(_local_detect, image)
        return {"source": "YOLO11s (local)", "ms": round((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000), "detections": dets}
    return {"source": None, "ms": 0, "detections": [], "error": "No detector connected. Set YOLO_URL or install ultralytics."}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Cosmos Reason (video Q&A)

_cosmos_model: str | None = None


async def _cosmos_model_id(client: httpx.AsyncClient, url: str, headers: dict) -> str:
    global _cosmos_model
    if env("COSMOS_MODEL"):
        return env("COSMOS_MODEL")
    if _cosmos_model is None:
        r = await client.get(f"{url}/v1/models", headers=headers, timeout=10)
        r.raise_for_status()
        _cosmos_model = r.json()["data"][0]["id"]
    return _cosmos_model


async def cosmos_answer(client: httpx.AsyncClient, claim: dict, question: str) -> dict | None:
    url = env("COSMOS3_REASON_URL")
    clip = ROOT / "poodle" / claim["footage"]["clip"]
    if not url or not clip.exists():
        return None
    url = url.rstrip("/")
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {env('COSMOS_TOKEN')}"} if env("COSMOS_TOKEN") else {}
    prompt = (
        "This is dashcam footage of a road collision, reviewed for an insurance claim. Answer the adjuster's question "
        "from what is visible only. If it cannot be seen, say it is not visible. "
        'Reply as <think>your reasoning</think><answer>{"answer": "<= 2 sentences", "grounded": true|false}</answer>.\n'
        f"Question: {question}"
    )
    video = base64.b64encode(clip.read_bytes()).decode()
    r = await client.post(f"{url}/v1/chat/completions", headers=headers, timeout=60, json={
        "model": await _cosmos_model_id(client, url, headers),
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": f"data:video/mp4;base64,{video}"}},
            {"type": "text", "text": prompt},
        ]}],
        "max_tokens": 400, "temperature": 0,
    })
    r.raise_for_status()
    text = r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    if "<answer>" in text:
        text = text.split("<answer>", 1)[1].split("</answer>", 1)[0].strip()
    try:
        body = json.loads(text)
        answer, grounded = body.get("answer", ""), bool(body.get("grounded"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        answer, grounded = text, not text.lower().startswith("not visible")
    return {"answer": answer, "grounded": grounded, "citations": []}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- W&B Inference (LLM prose)

async def llm_answer(client: httpx.AsyncClient, claim: dict, question: str) -> dict | None:
    key = env("WANDB_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        return None
    findings = [{"id": f["id"], "text": f["text"], "conf": f["conf"]} for f in claim["findings"]]
    prompt = (
        "You answer an insurance adjuster's question about incident footage using ONLY these findings. "
        "If the findings cannot answer it, say it is not visible. Reply as JSON: "
        '{"answer": "<= 2 sentences", "citations": ["finding ids"], "grounded": true|false}.\n'
        f"Findings: {json.dumps(findings)}\nQuestion: {question}"
    )
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}
    if env("WANDB_PROJECT"):
        headers["OpenAI-Project"] = env("WANDB_PROJECT")
    r = await client.post("https://api.inference.wandb.ai/v1/chat/completions", headers=headers, timeout=30, json={
        "model": env("POODLE_LLM_MODEL") or "meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "max_tokens": 220, "temperature": 0,
        "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
    })
    r.raise_for_status()
    body = json.loads(r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])
    return {"answer": body.get("answer", ""), "grounded": bool(body.get("grounded")),
            "citations": [{"finding": c} for c in body.get("citations", [])]}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Jev (typed coverage answers)

FAULT_OPTIONS = {
    "not_at_fault": "the policyholder did nothing to cause the collision",
    "shared_fault": "both drivers contributed",
    "mostly_at_fault": "the policyholder caused most of it",
    "fully_at_fault": "the policyholder caused it",
    "cannot_determine": "the facts do not show who caused it",
}


def jev_questions(policy: dict, wording: dict) -> dict:
    exclusions = {k: v["text"] for k, v in wording.items() if k.startswith("E")}
    exclusions["none"] = "no exclusion applies"
    return {
        "peril": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What happened in `facts`?", "criteria": {
            "collision_with_vehicle": "a collision with another vehicle", "collision_with_object": "hit an object",
            "collision_with_pedestrian_or_cyclist": "hit a person on foot or a cyclist", "theft": "theft",
            "vandalism": "vandalism", "fire": "fire", "weather": "weather damage", "glass_only": "glass only", "other": "something else"}},
        "section_covers_peril": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does Section 1 in `policy` cover damage to the policyholder's own car for this incident under `policy.cover`?"},
        "exclusion": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which exclusion in `policy` do `facts` trigger?", "criteria": exclusions},
        "fault_band": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "How much did the policyholder contribute to the collision in `facts`?", "criteria": FAULT_OPTIONS},
        "benefit_courtesy_car": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Would the policyholder need a courtesy car while their car is repaired, given `facts`?"},
```

```text
=====WATCH head=====
"""Background incident scanner: every live TfL JamCam, judged by Jev, kept as a library.

The app starts it when a Jev key is set (POODLE_WATCH=off turns it off):

- poll each camera's still with a conditional GET; S3 answers 304 until TfL publishes
  a new frame, which happens every 5 to 8 minutes per camera;
- send each new frame to Jev once, with every question below batched in one request;
- code turns the typed answers into incidents: opened by one flagged frame, confirmed
  by a second, cleared after two quiet frames or 30 minutes without a frame.

Runtime data lives in data/library/ (gitignored) and is served at /library/:
  observations-<date>.jsonl  one row per judged frame: the data mine
  incidents.json             the incident library
  frames/, clips/            incident stills and the camera's 10 s clips, with SHA-256
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import random
import time
import uuid
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, deque
from datetime import date, datetime
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from . import services, tfl

LIBRARY = Path(services.env("POODLE_LIBRARY_DIR") or Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "library")
USD_PER_TOKEN = 0.042 / 1_000_000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- questions and thresholds
# One reviewable place for what Jev is asked about each frame and how code acts on it.
# Thresholds are starting points from a probe on crash stills and live frames; calibrate
# them on the review labels the desk collects.

QUESTIONS = {

        "criteria": {"true": "the carriageway is visible clearly enough to judge what is happening on it",

    "incident": {

        "criteria": {"true": "a collision, a damaged, overturned or burning vehicle, a vehicle stopped across a live lane "
                             "or at an odd angle, emergency services working on the road, debris or a fallen object on "
                             "the carriageway, flooding, or a person lying in the road",
                     "false": "ordinary traffic, including queues, parked cars, buses at stops, vehicles waiting at lights, "
                              "roadworks behind barriers, and vehicles stopped at the kerb"}},
    "kind": {
        "type": "choice", "instructions": "What is the main thing happening on the road in `frame`?",
        "criteria": {
            "collision": "a crash: vehicles in contact, a damaged or overturned vehicle, or wreckage",
            "breakdown": "one vehicle stopped in a live lane with hazard lights, a raised bonnet or a tow truck",
            "emergency_response": "police, ambulance or fire vehicles stopped on the road at a scene",
            "obstruction": "debris, a fallen tree, a spilled load or another object blocking the carriageway",
            "flooding": "standing water covering part of the carriageway",
            "fire_or_smoke": "flames or smoke from a vehicle or the roadside",
            "person_in_road": "a person lying, standing or walking in a live traffic lane away from a crossing",
            "roadworks": "planned works: cones, barriers, works vehicles or a lane closed for maintenance",
            "congestion": "slow or stationary queues with no visible cause",
            "normal": "traffic moving normally, or an empty road",
            "unclear": "the frame is too dark, blurred, obstructed or blank to tell",
            "other": "something else unusual on the road"}},
    "severity": {
        "type": "score", "instructions": "How urgently should a traffic control room operator look at `frame`?",
        "criteria": ["nothing to act on: normal traffic",
                     "worth noting: a stopped vehicle, a queue or works that is not blocking traffic",
                     "act now: a lane is blocked by a collision, breakdown, obstruction or emergency scene",

    "emergency_vehicle": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is a police car, ambulance or fire engine visible in `frame`?"},
    "damaged_vehicle": {

    "lane_blocked": {

    "usable": 0.5,  # below: the view cannot be judged, so the frame neither extends nor clears an incident
    "open": 0.7,    # `incident` needed to open an incident, or to count towards confirming one
    "keep": 0.5,    # `incident` that keeps an open incident alive
    "box": 0.3,     # weakest box confidence worth drawing
}
INCIDENT_KINDS = {"collision", "breakdown", "emergency_response", "obstruction", "flooding", "fire_or_smoke",
                  "person_in_road", "other"}
CONFIRM_FRAMES = 2       # flagged frames that confirm an incident
CLEAR_FRAMES = 2         # quiet frames in a row that clear it
STALE_SECONDS = 30 * 60  # an open incident with no frame for this long is cleared
MAX_FRAMES = 12          # stills kept per incident
MAX_CLIPS = 3            # 10 s clips kept per incident
POLL_IDLE = 60           # seconds between checks while a camera's still is unchanged
POLL_AFTER_NEW = 210     # TfL refreshes each camera every 5 to 8 minutes
FETCH_CONCURRENCY = 12
```

```text
.env.example
# Poodle: API keys and service URLs
#
# Copy this file to .env and put the real values there:
#     cp .env.example .env
# .env is gitignored. This file is committed, and every commit is pushed to GitHub,
# so never put a real key in this file.
#
# Every value is optional. Leave one blank and that service runs in replay mode;
# the sidebar shows which services are live. Restart the server after editing .env.
# Variables already set in your shell or on the event VM take priority over .env.

# ---- TfL JamCams: live London traffic cameras --------------------------------
# Works without a key, but TfL rate-limits anonymous calls. Free key:
# https://api-portal.tfl.gov.uk (sign up, subscribe to the free product, copy the primary key).
TFL_APP_KEY=

# ---- YOLO on the event stack: detection on live camera stills ----------------
# URL and token from the team VM (lab docs or /config/<team>.config).
# Without them, scans use a local ultralytics install if there is one.
YOLO_URL=
YOLO_TOKEN=
# Local detector only: path to the weights file (default yolo11s.pt, downloaded on first use).
POODLE_YOLO_WEIGHTS=

# ---- NVIDIA Cosmos Reason on the event stack: answers questions from the video
# Base URL without /v1. Token only if the endpoint asks for one.
# COSMOS_MODEL is optional: Poodle reads the served model id from /v1/models.
COSMOS3_REASON_URL=
COSMOS_TOKEN=
COSMOS_MODEL=

# ---- W&B Inference on CoreWeave: answers in plain English when Cosmos is not set
# Key: https://wandb.ai/authorize   Project: <entity>/<project>
WANDB_API_KEY=
WANDB_PROJECT=
# Optional model override (default meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct).
POODLE_LLM_MODEL=

# ---- TypeSafe Jev: typed coverage answers (peril, exclusion, fault band) -----
# Set one of the two keys.
# TypeSafe: https://console.typesafe.ai/keys
# OpenRouter, no TypeSafe account needed: https://openrouter.ai/keys
TYPESAFE_API_KEY=
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
# Optional overrides. Defaults: jev-1.14.0 on TypeSafe, typesafe/jev-1.14 on OpenRouter.
JEV_MODEL=
JEV_BASE_URL=

# ---- Background incident scanner (server/watch.py) ---------------------------
# Runs whenever a Jev key is set: every live JamCam, each new still judged by Jev,
# about $0.50 an hour for all of London. Pause it from the desk, or set off here.
POODLE_WATCH=
# Scan only the N cameras nearest central London. Blank: all of them.
POODLE_WATCH_LIMIT=
# Stop scanning for the day once Jev spend reaches this many US dollars. Blank: no cap.
POODLE_WATCH_DAILY_USD=
# Parallel Jev requests (default 6).
POODLE_WATCH_CONCURRENCY=
# Where the incident library is kept (default server/data/library).
POODLE_LIBRARY_DIR=

# ---- VastDB: stores claim events (questions, approvals, attached stills) -----
# Endpoint and keys from the team VM. Needs: pip install vastdb pyarrow
# Without them, events go to server/data/events.jsonl only.
VASTDB_ENDPOINT=
VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY=
VASTDB_SECRET_KEY=
# Bucket for the poodle schema (default: poodle).
VASTDB_BUCKET=

# ---- Deploy only --------------------------------------------------------------
# Public URL of a bucket holding the contents of poodle/media/, to keep media out
# of a 1 MiB code deploy. Leave blank to serve media from this server.
POODLE_MEDIA_BASE=
```

````text
<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/screens/poodle-mark.svg" width="72" height="72" alt="Poodle logo">
</p>

<h1 align="center">Poodle</h1>

<p align="center">
  A claims desk for car accidents. Poodle watches the dashcam video, checks the driver's story<br>
  and works out what the policy pays. When it isn't sure, it hands the claim to a person.
</p>

<p align="center">
  Built in one day at the Real-Time Video Agents hackathon, VAST London, 17 October 2026.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="#a-quick-tour">Tour</a> ·
  <a href="#how-poodle-decides">How it decides</a> ·
  <a href="#run-it">Run it</a> ·
  <a href="#demo-in-90-seconds">Demo</a> ·
  <a href="#the-incident-library-in-more-detail">Incident library</a>
</p>

![A claim in Poodle. The dashcam clip is paused with a YOLO box on the car that pulled out, the nearest TfL cameras are on the right, and the recommendation is below.](docs/screens/claim.jpg)

## Why we built it

After a crash, an insurer has to answer a few questions. What happened? Who caused it? What does the policy cover? Today a claims handler works this out by hand, watching the video and checking the policy line by line.

Poodle does that first pass for them. It:

- spots the cars and traffic lights in the video, and writes down what happens moment by moment
- checks every sentence of the driver's statement against what the camera saw
- decides the cover with fixed rules, and shows the policy clause or Highway Code rule behind each reason
- puts the closest live London traffic cameras next to the evidence
- keeps a fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) of every file, so you can tell if anything changes later

A person still makes the call on anything unclear. Poodle tells them why it's unclear. (The poodle on each claim page has moods, by the way. It's happy when a claim can be paid and alert when a person should look.)

## A quick tour

### The inbox

![The inbox: seven claims waiting, each with its recommendation, amount and owner](docs/screens/inbox.jpg)

Claims that need a person come first. A row tells you what Poodle recommends, what the claim is worth and who owns it. Press `J` and `K` to move, and `Enter` to open one.

### A claim

The screenshot at the top of this page is a claim. The dashcam clip plays on the left. Click a finding under the video and the clip jumps to that moment, with boxes from YOLO (an object detector) on what it found. Below that, the recommendation shows what's covered, what isn't and how much gets paid now. The right side has the policy, a map, the rule checks and the evidence log.

### Checking the story

![The statement check marks "I was already on the roundabout" as contradicted. Below it are two answers about the footage.](docs/screens/statement-check.jpg)

Poodle breaks the driver's statement into small claims. It marks each one as supported, contradicted, or unverifiable when the video can't show it. In this claim the van driver says he was already on the roundabout. The motorcyclist's helmet camera shows he wasn't.

You can also ask the footage a question. Answers point to the finding they came from, or say "Not visible" when the video can't tell. Speed is a good example. One dashcam can't measure it, so Poodle won't guess.

### Live cameras

![Live TfL cameras, grouped by the claim they are near](docs/screens/cameras.jpg)

Every claim gets the four Transport for London (TfL) traffic cameras closest to it, with distances. London has about 800 of these cameras, and they post a new picture every 5 to 8 minutes.

![A live camera scanned with YOLO: 9 cars, 1 bus, 2 people and 3 traffic lights, next to an "Attach as evidence" button](docs/screens/live-scan.jpg)

Open a camera and scan its latest picture with YOLO. If it helps, attach it to a claim. The picture gets a fingerprint and goes into the claim's evidence log.

### The incident library

![The incident library: the scanner's latest pictures at the top, then incidents grouped into open and cleared](docs/screens/incident-library.jpg)

While the server runs, Poodle watches every TfL camera in London. New pictures go to Jev, a fast decision model from TypeSafe. Jev answers a fixed set of questions about each one: is there an incident, what kind, how bad, is a lane blocked, and so on. Code turns those answers into incidents. An incident keeps its pictures, the camera's 10-second video and every answer Jev gave.

![One incident: the camera picture with Jev's box around the problem, a strip of pictures and clips, Jev's answers and two review buttons](docs/screens/incident.jpg)

It makes mistakes. Low sun and dirty lenses can look like smoke to it. When that happens, click "Not an incident". Your reviews are saved with the incident, and we'll use them to tune it.

### The evidence pack

<img src="docs/screens/evidence-pack.jpg" width="560" alt="The printable evidence pack for claim PD-0147">

There's a one-page report for every claim, ready to print or send. It has the decision and the reasons, what's covered, the checks, the findings, the statement check and the fingerprint of every file.

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | What they do |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘K` | Search, or jump to any claim, camera or page |
| `J` / `K` | Move down / up the list |
| `Enter` | Open the selected claim |
| `Esc` | Go back to the list |
| `Space` | Play or pause the footage |
| `D` | Show or hide the detection boxes |
| `⌘Enter` | Approve the recommendation |
| `G` then `I`, `C`, `A` or `L` | Go to the inbox, cameras, all claims or the incident library |
| `?` | Show every shortcut |

## How Poodle decides

We split the work so each part does what it's good at.

- Code handles anything with one right answer: dates, money, whether the driver is named on the policy, and the decision table itself.
- Jev answers questions with a fixed list of possible answers. For example, it picks who caused the crash from five options. Every answer comes with a confidence score.
- A language model only writes sentences, like the answers to your questions about the footage.

Sometimes Poodle doesn't decide. It sends the claim to a person when Jev is less than 50% sure about an important answer, when there isn't enough evidence, or when the fraud signs are strong. The claim page says which one it was.

## Run it

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
cp .env.example .env    # optional: put API keys here (this file is never committed)
uv run --with-requirements server/requirements.txt uvicorn server.app:app --port 8080
```

Then open http://localhost:8080.

Every key is optional. Without them, Poodle uses recorded answers, so the demo always works. Restart the server after you change `.env`.

To scan live cameras with YOLO on your own laptop, run the server in an environment that also has `ultralytics`:

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12 && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r server/requirements.txt ultralytics
.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn server.app:app --port 8080
```

## What's live and what's recorded

Each service switches on when its key is in `.env`. Without the key, Poodle falls back to recorded data and keeps working.

| Part | Live with | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| London traffic cameras | No key needed (`TFL_APP_KEY` raises TfL's rate limit) | The last saved camera list |
| YOLO scan of a live camera | `YOLO_URL`, or `ultralytics` installed locally | The scan says no detector is connected |
| Boxes on the claim footage | Worked out ahead of time with YOLO11s (`server/tools/detect_stills.py`) | Same |
| Coverage decision | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (Jev) | Recorded Jev answers |
| Questions about the footage | `COSMOS3_REASON_URL` (Cosmos Reason) or `WANDB_API_KEY` (W&B Inference) | Answers built from the findings |
| Incident library | A Jev key | Off |
| Event store | `VASTDB_ENDPOINT`, `VASTDB_ACCESS_KEY` and `VASTDB_SECRET_KEY` | `server/data/events.jsonl` |

`.env.example` lists every setting, with a note on where to get each key.

## The incident library, in more detail

The scanner is in `server/watch.py`. Here's what it does.

1. About once a minute it asks each camera whether its picture has changed. A picture that hasn't changed costs nothing.
2. A new picture goes to Jev once, with 12 questions in a single request. Is there an incident? What kind? Is a lane blocked? Is the road wet? There are eight more like these, plus a box around the problem.
3. One picture that scores 0.7 or more, with an incident type such as a collision or a breakdown, opens an incident. A second picture confirms it.
4. Two quiet pictures in a row close it. So do 30 minutes with no new picture.

Every judged picture also goes into a daily log. That gives you road conditions and traffic for every camera in London, every few minutes. It all lives in `server/data/library/`, which isn't committed and is served at `/library/`.

| File | What's in it |
| --- | --- |
| `observations-<date>.jsonl` | One line per picture: camera, time, every answer, tokens used |
| `incidents.json` | The incident library (the Export button downloads it) |
| `frames/` and `clips/` | Incident pictures and 10-second clips, each with a SHA-256 hash |

Opened, confirmed, cleared and reviewed incidents also go to `events.jsonl`, and to VastDB once it's set up.

### What it costs

A picture costs about 1,700 Jev tokens, roughly $0.00007. All of London comes to about 7,000 pictures and $0.50 an hour.

### How to control it

Use the Pause button on the page. It stays paused after a restart. Or use these settings in `.env`:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `POODLE_WATCH=off` | Turns the scanner off |
| `POODLE_WATCH_LIMIT` | Scans only the N cameras nearest central London |
| `POODLE_WATCH_DAILY_USD` | Stops for the day once Jev spend reaches this many dollars |
| `POODLE_WATCH_CONCURRENCY` | How many Jev requests run at once (6 by default) |
| `POODLE_LIBRARY_DIR` | Keeps the library somewhere else, like a bigger disk |

### Why the threshold is 0.7

In a test, real crash pictures scored between 0.94 and 0.99. The highest normal London picture in the first sweep scored 0.63, and that was a smudged lens. So 0.7 sits in the gap. Some sun glare still gets through, which is why the review buttons are there. The questions and thresholds are all at the top of `server/watch.py`.

## Demo in 90 seconds

1. The inbox has seven claims that need a person. Open PD-0147 (`J`/`K`, then `Enter`).
2. The policyholder's dashcam plays. A blue Vauxhall Mokka pulls out of a give-way junction into her. Click the finding "Blue car broadside across the policyholder's lane" and the clip stops there, with a YOLO box on the car. The two nearest live TfL cameras sit beside it.
3. Ask "Where was the point of impact?" (the answer cites the impact finding). Then ask "How fast was the other car going?" (the answer is "Not visible").
4. The recommendation is accept, partial. The other driver is at fault under Highway Code rule 172, and the courtesy car isn't on her policy. Poodle pays £6,500 now and recovers £6,850 from the other insurer.
5. Open a live camera, scan its latest picture and attach it to the claim. It joins the evidence log with its fingerprint.
6. Press `⌘K` and type "camden". PD-0226 (hit from behind in traffic) can be paid without a handler. PD-0188 (a car cut in from a slip road, then braked hard) has a fraud flag and goes to the special investigations team. In PD-0204 the van driver says he was already on the roundabout, and the rider's helmet camera says he wasn't.
7. Press `G` then `L` for the incident library: the scanner's live feed and the incidents it found today.
8. Open the evidence pack: one printable page with the decision, the findings, the statement check and the file fingerprints.

The amounts in steps 4 and 6 come from the recorded Jev answers. See the next section.

## What doesn't work yet

- Live Jev is stricter than the recorded answers. With a Jev key set, it sends most claims to a person for now.
- The incident scanner has false alarms, mostly sun glare and dirty lenses.
- The Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB connections are written but not tested. We didn't have those credentials on the laptop we built this on.

## Where the footage comes from

The claim videos are real UK dashcam and helmet-camera clips sent in to UK Dash Cameras. The originals are in `poodle/media/raw/` (about 90 MB). `server/tools/build_media.py` cuts them into 720p web clips with posters (about 16 MB). The findings, statement checks and Jev answers were written for each clip. The places, dates, people and policies are made up, so the dates burned into the videos don't match the claims.

Live camera pictures come from TfL JamCams. Powered by TfL Open Data.

We also tried generating crash clips. `server/tools/luma_videos.py` makes 5-second CCTV-style clips with Luma Ray2 on Amazon Bedrock, with the camera locked in place. The desk doesn't use them. It plays the real footage. Ray2 only runs in us-west-2, costs $7.50 per clip and needs `aws sso login`.

## Deploying

The code is small, but the video isn't. To keep the media out of a small deploy, upload `poodle/media/` to a bucket and set `POODLE_MEDIA_BASE` to its URL.

## Project layout

```text
server/               FastAPI backend (port 8080)
  app.py              API routes, and serves the web app
  engine.py           hard rules, the decision table, offline answers
  services.py         YOLO, Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference, Jev and VastDB
  tfl.py              the TfL camera list
  watch.py            the background scanner and incident library
  tools/              build the clips, precompute YOLO boxes, Luma clips
  data/               claims, policies and detections (runtime files are not committed)
poodle/               the web app: plain JavaScript modules, no build step
docs/                 the idea, the hack plan, the UI audit and these screenshots
agent-coordination/   the shared taskboard for coding agents
```

Built with FastAPI, TfL JamCams, YOLO11 from Ultralytics, TypeSafe Jev, NVIDIA Cosmos Reason, W&B Inference and VastDB.

More reading: [the idea and agent design](docs/IDEA.md), [the hack plan](docs/hack-plan.md) and [the UI audit](docs/ui-audit.md).

## Working on this repo with coding agents

This repo was set up with `hackathon-init`. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) share one taskboard: [`agent-coordination/taskboard.md`](agent-coordination/taskboard.md). Each agent writes down what it's building, saves progress as it goes, and can pick up a task another agent left half done.

Every turn starts by pulling from GitHub, in case someone else pushed. Every commit is pushed straight away. After you clone, turn that on once:

```bash
./scripts/agent-taskboard.sh setup
```
````

````text
## Problem

- Motor claims depend on "he said / she said". Video exists more often than ever (dashcams, doorbells, shop CCTV, phones), but adjusters still scrub through it by hand.
- Clips arrive from different devices, with different clocks, angles and quality. Nobody lines them up.
- Liability depends on context the video alone doesn't show: junction layout, signal phases, speed limits, give-way lines, the Highway Code.
- Even once fault is clear, the adjuster still has to read the policy: is this peril covered under the customer's cover level, does an exclusion apply, which benefits (courtesy car, windscreen, legal expenses, personal injury) kick in, what is the excess. This is slow, inconsistent between handlers, and hard to explain to the customer.
- Fraud (staged "crash-for-cash" collisions) costs insurers heavily and is hard to spot without frame-level review.
- Evidence used in disputes or court needs proof it hasn't been altered, plus a clear trail of how conclusions were reached.

## How everything ties together

```
          ┌─────────────────────────── Claim submitted ────────────────────────────┐
          │  videos · GPS/IMU · statements (text/voice) · policy schedule + wording │

                                            │
            ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
            ▼                               ▼                               ▼
    Perception Agent                    Sync Agent                    Context Agent
 YOLO11s detect + track,          anchor events + audio →        OpenStreetMap, Mapillary /
 impact, Jev frame checks,        one incident clock             Street View, Highway Code
 VSS + Cosmos3-Reason + Embed1                                    (Jev picks rule)
            └───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┘
                                            ▼
                               Reconstruction Agent
                      (map positions, speeds, bird's-eye replay)
                                            │
       ┌──────────────────┬─────────────────┼──────────────────┬──────────────────┐
       ▼                  ▼                 ▼                  ▼                  ▼
   Q&A Agent      Statement & Fraud    Liability Agent   Coverage & Benefits   Report Agent
````
